title: Cast iron seasoning is a myth, seriously.
body: I've been using cast iron for years and I just want to say people are totally wrong about the care. You don't need to scrub it down with harsh soap every time you cook. That just wears down the seasoning layer. A light wipe with a damp cloth and letting it air dry is all you need. Letting it breathe is actually part of the process. Don't overcomplicate it; just treat it gently and let the food flavor the surface naturally.

title: My secret to perfect cooked rice
body: I've been trying to master cooking rice and I finally figured out a trick that works for me. The biggest mistake I used to make was not letting the rice sit and steam properly after adding the water. Now, I always let the rice rest, covered, for about ten minutes after taking it off the heat before fluffing it with a fork. This gives it that perfect fluffy texture every single time. It really makes a difference when you're just starting out.
